title: End-to-End Parametric Portfolio Policies — Transformer vs TSMOM on CME Futures
content:
New wiki page at wiki/trading/algorithms/e2e-portfolio-policies.md covering Pollok & Robik (2026) arXiv:2607.00475.

Key findings:
- End-to-end transformer policy (market state → weights via differentiable Sharpe loss) matches or exceeds TSMOM on 16 CME futures after transaction costs
- LSTM has higher gross Sharpe but 3-5x higher turnover, is cost-killed net
- Transformer learns to trade infrequently — attention mechanism concentrates on durable regime signals
- Sub-asset finding: AI models add most value on equity index futures; commodity futures already well-captured by simple TSMOM (validates H261b approach)
- H318 implication: use transformer attention patterns as features for meta-learner, not as direct policy (sample-size too small for monthly ETF data)
- Design note: differentiable Sharpe loss + transformer architecture is the correct template for any end-to-end trading policy work

Page created at wiki/trading/algorithms/e2e-portfolio-policies.md (circa 600 words with implementation notes and cross-refs).
